CLIMATE ACTION 
Climate Action Plan (CAP) 
1. Met REVAMP (Longford) social enterprise circular economy hub on model of funding repair of goods 
and materials (6 August 2025).  Directive on repair of goods important in requiring design of goods to 
mobilise the circular repair economy. 
2. Met Atlantic Technological University (ATU) (12 August 2025) on partnering for EU HORIZON climate 
adaptation funding.  Number of partners including Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown.  Agreed to partner, 
topic of adaptation to be defined later in the application. 
3. Met with ATU and Sligo Leitrim Energy Agency (SLEA) (14 August 2025) on advancing retrofit numbers 
in Co. Leitrim.  Agreed to run 2 no campaigns, Carrick-on-Shannon during CA Week and 
Manorhamilton later in the year.  SLEA recommend an additional director from Leitrim.  A wider 
meeting needed with all SLEA stakeholders on scope. 
4. Organising events for CA week ongoing (aligned with An Tasice designation, 13 – 19 October 2025).  
Met ATU Careers department (21 August 2025) re their STEM Day on 15 October 2025.  Opened 
dialogue with MSL ETB on the Green Accelerator Skills Programme (GRASP) (28 August 2025) on 
collaboration, good alignment with the Programme and the LA CAPs.  MSL ETB to take up a stand at 
the ATU STEM Day. 
5. New Climate Action Officer, Oliver Wynne (start 20 August 2025). 
6. Met with The Dock (21 August 2025) on Climate Café, agreed preparation for early in 2026.  The Dock 
to facilitate CA Week event for Leitrim Sustainable Agriculture Group.  Leitrim CC CA support for the 
Dock, added them to the DZ taskforce (Carrick-on-Shannon Climate Action SEC). 
7. Comments made on draft Lot(i) of the feasibility study on District Heating by AECOM.  Lot (i) claim to 
be made with Cavan & Monaghan LAs through Pathfinder Programme.  Lot(ii) focus on on Carrick-on-
Shannon, funding to be discussed with SEAI. 
8. Go Car contributing trips for trees on bookings made on National carpool day (24 July 2025).  Leitrim 
CC agreed that any trees could go to the national location (2 no trees). 
 
Community Climate Action Programme Fund 
Date for opening of calls for Phase 2 is to be confirmed, Department stated LAs will be given 6 weeks notice 
before opening.  Department confirmed the call would be for Strand 1 only (Strand 1a cross border 
community climate action will not be rolled out initially). 
 
Biodiversity  
National Heritage Week (16 – 24 August): A programme of public events was organised, promoted and 
delivered across Co. Leitrim. Biodiversity events included online webinars & public walks and talks in 
Carrick on Shannon & Manorhamilton.  
 
Return to Nature (LBAF funded project):  
The aim of the project is to create biodiversity-friendly spaces on church grounds. Parishes are 
encouraged to transform 30% of their grounds into areas that support biodiversity. The project has 
started with 4 different parishes/communities in Co. Leitrim.

COMMUNITY AND INTEGRATION 
Local Enhancement Programme 2025 
On 13th June 2025, the Department of Rural and Community Development and an Gaeltacht announced 
€114,782.86 for 148 projects in Co Leitrim under the Local Enhancement Programme 2025. All payments 
have been made under the current stream which supports groups with bills (energy, broadband, 
insurance bills etc.). 
Groups have completed the Acceptance of Offer under the Capital stream with 11 drawdown 
submissions received to date. 
 
Age Friendly Programme   
Work continues to merge the Age Friendly Ireland (AFI) Business Training programme and the HSE’s 
Dementia Understand Together business training into one programme. The aim is to deliver one 
programme to businesses, satisfying the requirements of both AFI and HSE and remove duplication in 
service delivery from separate agencies. Both AFI and the HSE are supportive of this pilot in Leitrim. 
Nursing Home Pilot Project: Personal plans for residents are complete in Lough Erril & Arus Breffni with 
50% of personal plans complete in Arus Carolan. Personal plans for residents will then start in the three 
remaining nursing homes in Leitrim. 
Healthy Ireland 
Healthy Ireland continue to work along with Sharon Richardson (HSE) on the roll out of ‘Understanding 
Together – Dementia Friendly Leitrim’. Following a presentation in Breffni FRC on Thursday 14th August a 
working group was created to roll out Dementia Friendly Carrick. A date of October 1st has been chosen 
for the Community Information night, after which there will be community training.

6 
 
Community Recognition Fund 
Leitrim has been allocated over €2.2 million under this funding programme, which will be invested 
across 16 capital projects throughout the county. All successful applicants have now received their 
letters of offer, and work is actively underway on each of the approved projects.  
 
Love Where You Live 
The Love Where You Live Competition recognises and celebrates the valuable contributions made by 
community and voluntary groups, as well as schools, throughout County Leitrim.  Judging across all five 
categories has now been completed. Final preparation for delivering the awards night is almost 
complete.

Leitrim PEACEPLUS Action Plan (1.1) 
Local Community Regeneration & Transformation 
• Project Management services are currently being procured for the Play & Art Therapy Facility in 
Drumkeeran and the MUGA in Ballinamore.  
• Construction tender deadline for Coleman’s was extended by one week to 26th August 2025. 
• Currently preparing Request for Quotations for projects in Kinlough & Lurganboy 
 
Thriving & Peaceful Communities  
• Tender currently out for a Practical Skills Training Programme to work with those affected by 
legacy of The Troubles and other displaced persons. This programme will include tractor skills, 
first aid, quad bike certification among others. 
• Quotations have also been sought for a Volunteer Support Programme to deliver training to those 
using volunteers and volunteers themselves.  
 
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena (1.4) 
McAdam Design are continuing to work on the Design of the Shannonside Peace Arena and preparing the 
tender package for the entire campus. 
There have been significant delays with the LSSIF funding from the Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, 
Sport and Media. We are still awaiting to progress through Approval Gateway 1 as per the Infrastructure 
Guidelines issued by the DPER. This is a mandatory requirement of the funding and the project cannot 
progress to tender stage until approved. 
 
Local Community Safety Partnership (LCSP) 
The Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, has commenced. We are currently awaiting the 
accompanying regulations which will provide a framework for establishing the Local Community Safety 
Partnership in line with the provisions of the Act. 
In accordance with the legislation the membership of the LCSP will be community focused. Statutory 
services including AGS, HSE, TUSLA and seven local Councillors will be mandated onto the LCSP. Further 
members will be recruited on local needs.

Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
The Integration Team conducted 6 clinics in the month of August. One clinic focused on Beneficiaries of 
Temporary Protection, and five clinics were held between Abbey Manor Hotel, and Carraig 
Accommodation IPAS centres. All clinics were to identify the needs residences/families. 
 
Two Offer a Home activations were completed in August accommodating 12 individuals. 
 
The Local Authority Integration Team worked in partnership with Foróige, and part funded integration 
camps for young people aged 10 – 17 years in Dromahair and Ballinamore. A total of 29 children avail of 
the programmes. 
 
The Integration Team are currently working in partnership with Leitrim County Childcare Committee, 
Leitrim Sports Partnership and Lifestart on the development of a two-tier programme. The programme 
will provide support to parents through a structured parenting initiative, while children under the age of 
five who are not participating in the Early Childhood Care and Education scheme will engage in a multi-
activity sports programme.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
 
 
 
There were over 9,000 visitors to the libraries across the county and there were 209 new members who 
joined Leitrim library Service in July. 
National Heritage Week 
To celebrate National Heritage Week 2025, the Local Studies Librarian hosted a very special event in 
conjunction with Scéal Heritage Consultancy, as part of the overall project Leitrim Women through time, 
entitled 'voices from the factory floor' on 9th August.  25 women who were former factory workers in 4 
Leitrim factories attended.  Their memories were recorded and an exhibition will be prepared along with 
an audio and visual display and a follow up event will take place in November. 
In Dromahair library on Tuesday 19th Dromahair native Tony Downey performed live readings from his 
popular podcast 'Leitrim to Birmingham'. On Friday 22nd of August Dromahair Library hosted the launch

9 
 
of the O'Rourke Trail map of Leitrim designed by exploring in collaboration with the Leitrim County 
Council Heritage Officer Sarah Malone. 
 
Summer Stars  
778 children participated in the library’s annual Reading Programme. Children enjoyed a range of events 
to support this national initiative such as story times, craft workshops etc. Almost 10,500 children’s 
books were borrowed during the 3 month period June to August. 
 
Community Engagement  
Our libraries continue to serve as vibrant and inclusive spaces for community connection and lifelong 
learning.  Dromahair Library was used as a meeting space by local community groups such as the 
Dromahair Town Team Committee and Heritage Committee.  Ballinamore Library welcomed the 
inaugural meeting of the Ballinamore area Friends of Breastfeeding group on August 26th. This group 
now meets weekly, offering support and connection for local parents. 
 
Exhibition 
Leitrim Gaelic Games – Reflections and Memories’ exhibition was on display in Ballinamore Library from 
12th to 16th August during the Ballinamore Festival. This exhibition celebrates the rich history and impact 
of Gaelic Games on our communities here in Leitrim. Through the exhibition boards, various elements of 
Gaelic Games across the county were highlighted. Many people visited the library to view this resource.

Digital Strategy 
A copy of the draft digital strategy was issued to elected members in August ahead of the Council 
meeting on Sept 1st. 
 
Broadband Connection Points – Upgrade of BCP equipment.   
The upgrade of the BCP equipment for the 12 BCP sites in Leitrim commenced in August 2025. 
 
Carrick Business Campus 
A Feasibility Study on a proposed new Smart Technology Hub in the Carrick Business Campus has 
concluded. The Study is funded by the Enterprise Ireland Smart Regions Enterprise Innovation Fund.  
 
County Promotion 
Work is ongoing in terms of finalising plans, invitees list etc for the Intercounty Promotion Event on Nov 
27th at the Irish Embassy in London.  
Planning is ongoing for the Smart Towns and Village Conference due to be held or October 2025. 
Planning continues for the forthcoming “Powering Up – Scaling for Impact” event at Carrick Campus, 
scheduled for 3rd October. 
 
Leitrim Diaspora 
Public consultation meetings were held in Ballinamore, Carrick-on-Shannon, and Manorhamilton, with 
an additional online session provided specifically for elected members. An online survey was also 
available from 1st to 31st August, allowing broader public input. In the coming weeks, feedback from all 
consultation channels will be analysed to inform the development of the new Diaspora Strategy 
framework. 
   
Leitrim Economic Forum and Global Business Network 
The next meeting of the Economic Forum is scheduled for 24th September.  The Economic Forum 
working groups — the Leitrim Skills Strategy Working Group and the Invest in Leitrim Business Summit 
Working Group — are scheduled to take place in September and October 2025 respectively. 
 
DRCD Funded Schemes 
Minister Calleary announced the successful Measure 1 and Project Development projects during August. 
Leitrim have received a funding offer on seven projects in total, two Project Development and five 
Measure 1 projects.  
 
TOURISM 
Autum Campaign 
Scheduled to run from September through October, the campaign will feature a comprehensive mix of 
media channels, including radio, video-on-demand, digital platforms, and press. The aim is to maximise 
visibility and engagement across key audiences, with tailored messaging designed to resonate 
throughout the season. All creative assets and scheduling are being finalised to ensure a strong and 
coordinated launch.

11 
 
Consumer shows 
The Tourism Team attended Irish Fest in Milwaukee, which had an audience of over 150,000. It was the 
ideal opportunity to showcase Leitrim and Ireland as a holiday destination for our Leitrim Diaspora and 
people in the USA who are interested in Ireland. During the event, the Tourism Team met with Paul 
McDonagh, Tourism Ireland Trade & Industry Engagement Manager USA, who provided insights into 
Tourism Ireland's marketing plans for 2026 and the Irish Ambassador to the USA, Geraldine Byrne Nason. 
 
Mid Ulster Meeting  
The tourism team were part of a productive meeting with representatives from Mid Ulster Council.  The 
session included a recap of the recent visit by Leitrim County Council, followed by a constructive 
discussion around the potential for collaboration and mutually beneficial partnerships. An overview of 
the Glenfarne Wood project was provided, including its current status and the next phase of 
development. The meeting concluded with a focused conversation on partnership opportunities and 
how both councils can align efforts on some joint initiatives. 
 
LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher.  The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a SEAI 
Energy Audit.  The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up to a 
maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software. 
 
Atlantic Economic Corridor Update:  
Interreg Europe Digital Rural 
On Monday 13th October 2025 a national conference will be held in Lough Rynn Castle on the topic of 
Smart Town and Villages. Minister Dara Calleary, Justin Gleeson from AIRO and Dr Karen Keavney from 
UCD are amongst the confirmed speakers.  Following the conference partners from the Digital Rural 
project will then spend two days in Leitrim attending presentations and site visits for various projects 
and initiatives.

A multi-agency supported tender package went out on e-tenders which will explore the opportunities

represented on the project by Director of Economic Development and the NW Programme Manager.

TOWN REGENERATION 
Croí Conaithe – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant  
The Croí Cónaithe initiative aims to revitalise vacant and derelict properties by converting them into 
family homes and rental residential units. The Vacant Homes Officer continues to work closely with 
applicants to identify and support the reuse of suitable properties. 
 
Between April and August 2025, 55 new applications were received, bringing the total number of 
applications from January to August 2025 to 84. During this reporting period, 26 grant payments were 
processed, relating to applications submitted in 2023 and 2024. 
 
Turning Vacant Properties into Cosy Homes Event 
Leitrim County Council hosted an Information Event to showcase the potential to transform vacant and 
derelict properties in County Leitrim into vibrant homes. The event took place on Thursday, 19th June 
2025 from 3pm to 8pm in the Landmark Hotel, Carrick-On-Shannon, Co. Leitrim and was very well 
attended. Almost 300 people attended the event and 30 exhibitors from the financial, building and 
construction, home improvement and auctioneering sectors showcased their wares and services. The 
Keynote speaker on the day was Award Winning Architect Hugh Wallace, who spoke about the benefits of 
refurbishing the existing housing stock in the country and the benefits that it brings in restoring vibrancy 
to towns and villages.  Other speakers on the day included: Anne Marie O’Connor from the Vacant Homes 
Unit of The Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, Shane Mulvey, Vacant Homes Officer 
Leitrim County Council, Mel Galvin, R&D Co-ordinator, Sligo ATU and Chief Executive of Leitrim Council, 
Joseph Gilhooly. Colin Regan performed the role of MC and chaired informative panel discussions with the 
speakers and previous grant applicants namely; Ciara Reynolds and John & Amanda O'Connell, who 
shared their experience of renovating an older property and applying for and availing of the Croí Cónaithe 
grant. 
 
Town Teams 
The Town Regeneration Officer and the Vacant Homes Officer continue to engage with town teams on 
general issues, town team governance and structure issues.  
 
Manorhamilton Town Centre First Plan 
On 14th August, Contractor Studio Myco and the town regeneration team held a community engagement 
event in the Bee Park Community Centre, supported by an online survey, to gather final feedback on the 
latest draft proposals for the Town Centre First Plan. The responses are now being analysed and collated 
by Studio Myco, with the final draft plan due to be completed in early October. 
 
THRIVE - Town Centre First Heritage Revival Scheme – Application Strand 1 & 2 
Leitrim County Council successfully secured funding under Strand 1 to carry out a feasibility study on the 
Town Hall Building in Carrick on Shannon to establish an end use for the building following widespread

a sustainable and viable reuse of Heritage buildings, in line with Town Centre First Approach. Following a 
widespread consultation process, a Part 8 application was approved by the Elected Members on 12th May

HOUSING, PLANNING, CORPORATE SERVICES AND TRANSFORMATION DIRECTORATE 
 
HOUSING  
Housing Allocations   
Applications and Assessments   
To date in 2025, the Housing Department has received a total of 117 new applications for social housing 
support.  Of these, 80 have been assessed – with 63 accepted and 17 refused.    25 applications are 
currently undergoing assessment, while 12 have been deemed invalid and require further information. 
There are currently 500 approved applicants on the housing waiting list. 
 
New Tenancies To date in 2025:   
A total of 21 new tenancies under the Local Authority and Approved Housing Body (AHB) housing 
programmes have commenced during 2025 to date. These tenancies represent newly allocated homes 
provided to applicants from the housing waiting list, offering long-term, secure accommodation under 
social housing supports.    
 
Traveller Accommodation Programme 2025–2029 
The Traveller Accommodation Programme 2025–2029, effective from 1st January 2025, outlines a five-
year target for the delivery of 20 No. accommodation units.  
As of 31st August 2025, a total of 6 No. units (representing a 30% achievement rate over the 5-year target) 
have been provided under the Standard Local Authority Housing Scheme.  Three additional units were 
delivered during the month of August. The Housing Department continues to work toward meeting the 
programme’s targets over the five-year period. 
 
Housing Grants   
Housing Grant Approvals and Payments  
During 2025, activity under the Housing Adaptation Grant schemes has remained strong, with a steady 
flow of approvals, payments, and applications under assessment. The following data provides an 
overview of progress to date and illustrates how the programme is supporting people to live 
independently at home in line with the Housing Disability Strategy. 
 
Expenditure to Date 
To date in 2025, a total of €474,146 has been paid out under the Housing Grants Programme, covering 88 
individual grants. This expenditure reflects: 
• 
54 Housing Adaptation Grants for People with a Disability (HGD), 
• 
24 Mobility Aids Grants (MAG), and 
• 
10 Housing Aid for Older People (HOP). 
 
Committed Expenditure  
At present, a total of €812,336.24 has been approved under the Housing Grants Programme but has not 
yet been drawn down by applicants. This covers 124 individual grants, broken down as follows: 
• 
57 Housing Adaptation Grants for People with a Disability (HGD), 
• 
16 Mobility Aids Grants (MAG), and

17 
 
• 
11 Housing Aid for Older People (HOP). 
 
These approvals represent a significant pipeline of works that, once completed and claimed, will further 
advance the objectives of the Housing Strategy for Disabled People by enabling greater independence, 
accessibility, and quality of life for those supported through the scheme. 
 
Applications Under Assessment 
In addition to the approvals already issued, we also have a pipeline of new applications currently under 
assessment. These include 39 Housing Aid for Older People applications, 9 Mobility Aids applications and 
12 Housing Adaptation Grants for People with a Disability.  
 
Summary 
Taken together, this level of investment under the Housing Grants Programme demonstrates the 
Council’s ongoing commitment to supporting people with disabilities and older persons to remain living 
independently at home. The grants are directly aligned with the objectives of the Housing Strategy for 
Disabled People 2022–2027, by facilitating essential adaptations and improvements that promote 
accessibility, safety, and dignity in the home environment. 
 
Social Housing Rent Review – 2025 
The rent review process for approximately 1,600 local authority and leasing tenancies remains ongoing. 
While overall progress has been gradual this month, the following activities have continued: 
• Assessment of Household Income: Preliminary findings indicate that revised rent levels are likely 
to increase in many cases due to higher reported household incomes. 
• Data Validation: The Rent Review Team is systematically verifying and updating household 
composition and occupancy records within the iHouse system to ensure accuracy.

Housing Acquisition Programme 2025 
The total allocation for the Housing Acquisition Programme in 2025 is €2,000,000. Outstanding 
commitments carried forward from previous years amount to €976,957, leaving a remaining balance of 
€1,023,043 available for new acquisitions in 2025. This funding will be targeted to address urgent local 
situations where households in receipt of social housing support are at risk of homelessness, or where 
there is an immediate need to acquire a property to meet a specific housing requirement. Funding will 
be allocated strictly to the following priority categories: 
• Tenancy Sustainment – Tenant in Situ (TIS) 
• Exits from homeless services 
• Urgent housing for people with a disability and older persons 
• Buy and Renew (B&R) acquisitions to address vacancy 
 
Revised eligibility criteria now apply to all new applications under the Tenant in Situ Scheme. For 
example, a property must have been in receipt of social housing support payments for a continuous 
period of at least two years to qualify.

• Heritage Week took place from 16th - 24th August with 31 no. events taking place across Leitrim. All

the Glen Centre; the launch of the O’Rourke’s of Leitrim Trail map; and an event celebrating traditional
